Three months after my husband died, my best friends invited me over for wine and told me they'd quietly moved on without me. "We already gave your cabin to someone else. That trip was really you and Tom's chapter." I smiled. I understand.
For twelve years, Tom and I cruised the Mediterranean every September with the same three couples. Cassie and Greg. Pam and Dave. Mike and his wife Julie, who passed the year before Tom did.
It was our thing. We'd plan it together over wine at Cassie's kitchen table every January. Book by March. Spend all summer looking forward to it.
I researched the ports for the group, hidden restaurants, private tours, walking routes that avoided the crowded spots. Tom carried the bags, dealt with the check-in agents, and handled the taxis at every port. He liked doing it. He was good at it.
Tom died fourteen months ago. Pancreatic cancer. Six weeks from the diagnosis to the funeral. He was 61.
The last real conversation we had was about the cruise. He was sitting up in the hospital bed and he said, "You'll still go, right? Suse, promise me." I told him of course I would. He nodded and closed his eyes and I don't think he heard me say the rest.
After the funeral, the calls came constantly. Cassie checking in every night. Pam dropping off casseroles. Everyone saying "let us know if you need anything."
By month three, the calls slowed down.
By month six, they stopped.
